body.p: Please reconsider the present application in view of the above amendments and the following remarks. Applicant thanks the Examiner for carefully considering the present application.
I. Disposition of Claims
Claim 1 has been amended. Support can be found at least in paragraphs [0014], [0042] and [0073] of the publication document.
Claim 11 has been amended in the manner similar to claim 1.
Claims 4-5, 8, and 16 have been amended in light of the amendments to their base claim and/or to improve their form.
No new matters are added.
II. Double-Patenting Rejection

In section 2 of the Office Action, claims 1-18 were rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-14 of US Patent No. 11,717,183 and 1-24 of US Patent No.10,898,109.

Applicant respectfully submits that the independent claims have been amended such that they are now distinct and maintain a clear demarcation over the claims 1-14 of US Patent No. 11,717,183 and 1-24 of US Patent No.10,898,109. As such, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection. III. Rejections under 35 U.S.C. §103
Claims 1-18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Weng (US5588435) in view of Yamauchi (US2002102023).
Amended claim 1 recites, among other elements:
automatically determining, by a processor of an ultrasound imaging device, a

section type of the specified section image based on one or more characteristics defined by the gray values of the pixels, the section type identifying a particular section of a particular area of the tissue from which the specified section image was acquired
automatically identifying at least one measurement item which is measurable in
the specified section image according to the section type of the specified section image
> Regarding Feature A

In section 7 of the Office Action, the Examiner conceded that Weng does not disclose automatically determining a section type of the specified section image based on one or more characteristics defined by the gray values of the pixels, the section type identifying a particular section of a particular area of the tissue from which the specified section image was acquired.
That is, Weng fails to disclose Feature A of the amended claim 1.

In section 8 of the Office Action, it was asserted that Yamauchi disclose automatically determining a section type of the specified section image based on one or more characteristics defined by the gray values of the pixels, the section type identifying a particular section of a particular area of the tissue from which the specified section image was acquired (which is similar to Feature A of the amended claim 1). Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Yamauchi discloses "After the image generating unit 110 and the image normalizing unit 111 generate a new ultrasound image, the automatic contour extracting unit 120 automatically extracts a contour of an object to be examined" (see paragraph [0103]). That is, the automatic contour extracting unit is used to extract a contour from the ultrasound image.
However, Yamauchi fails to disclose that the automatic contour extracting unit can automatically determine the section type of the object in the ultrasound image.

On the contrary, applicant respectfully submits that the type of the object in the ultrasound image has already been determined before the automatic contour extracting unit begins to operate. Specifically, paragraphs [0170], [0175] and [0178] of Yamauchi disclose: "This image normalizing unit 211 is unique in that it performs different normalization for each object to be examined, and that it selects a conversion operation best suited for the object and performs the selected conversion operation to normalize an ultrasound image of the object. The image normalizing unit 211 includes a control judging unit 211a, a standard storing unit 211b, and a density converting unit 211c", "On receiving an ultrasound image from the image generating unit 110, the control Judging unit 211a specifies an object to be examined and a region to be normalized in accordance with either an instruction given by the operator beforehand", and "This image normalizing unit 211 performs not fixed normalization but flexible normalization by selecting normalization best suited to an object to be examined. This allows subsequent image processing, such as contour extraction, to be accurately

performed at higher speed". That is, the object to be processed in the image has already been specified and selected according to the instruction given by the operator before the automatic contour extracting unit extracts the contour of the object.
Therefore, Yamauchi fails to disclose that the automatic contour extracting unit can automatically determine the section type of the object in the ultrasound image.

In view of the above, it is submitted that Yamauchi fails to disclose "automatically determining, by a processor of an ultrasound imaging device, a section type of the specified section image based on one or more characteristics defined by the gray values of the pixels, the section type identifying a particular section of a particular area of the tissue from which the specified section image was acquired," as recited in the amended claim 1.
> Regarding Feature B

In section 6 of the Office Action, it was asserted that Weng discloses identifying at least one measurement item corresponding to the specified section image based on the gray values of the pixels and measuring a measurement parameter of the specified section image based on the measurement item identified. (which is similar to Feature B of the amended claim 1). Applicant respectfully submits that Weng fails to disclose Feature B of the amended claim 1 for the following reasons.

Applicant respectfully submits that the "measurement item" refers to the items to be measured during the ultrasound examination, and different examination modes may include different measurement items. For example, in an abdomen mode, the common measurement items include the size of the liver, gallbladder, spleen and kidneys, etc. In an obstetric mode, head circumference (HC), biparietal diameter (BPD), abdominal circumference (AC) and femur length (FL) are necessary measurement items for each examination.

Weng merely teaches automatically measuring values of designated parameters. However, "automatically measuring something" is totally different from "automatically identifying what is/are to be measured". As a matter of fact, Weng (see col. 2, lines 30-40) explicitly discloses "The user then designates a general geometry feature of the displayed body structure and at least one measurement parameter associated with the designated geometry feature. For curved, closed structures such as the head or abdomen, the measurement parameters may, for example, be the HC, AC, OFD, or BPD". That is, in Weng, the measurement parameter(s) (which corresponds to the measurement items of the present invention) is designated by the user, rather than being identified automatically. In other words, in Weng, the user designates what is/are to
be measured, and then the processor automatically measures the values of the designated measurement parameter(s).

Therefore, it is submitted that Weng fails to disclose "automatically identifying at least one measurement item which is measurable in the specified section image according to the section type of the specified section image" as recited in the amended claim 1.
Furthermore, it is submitted that Yamauchi also fails to cure the above deficiencies of Weng.

In view of the foregoing, it is submitted that the cited references, considered separately or in combination, fail to disclose, teach or suggest Feature A and Feature B of amended claim 1, and amended claim 1 is therefore patentable over the cited references.

In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that amended claim 1 is patentable over the cited references. Based on the same reasons, amended claim 11 is also patentable over the cited references. Their respectively associated dependent claims are patentable by virtue of their dependency. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection under 35 U.S.C. §103.
In view of the foregoing amendments and remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application and the timely allowance of the pending claims.
